flags.why: Copies the text's "(E.S.E, 4, ..." exactly. The print reads "E.S.E.,", so the transcription dropped a stop. "E.S.E. to E.N.E." is the checker's merge and can't be copied as one string.
The text reads "E.S.E, 4, to E.N.E., 7". "4 to 7" isn't a printed string; the copy rule forbids that tidying, so "4" is right.
The text reads "6th, at Butt of Lewis" and the record copies it. The checker reads "26th" in the print, so the transcription dropped the "2".
The eighty were among the "flocks... going N.E.", so passing holds. But "The second flock rested about ten minutes on island" also merits a separate settled observation, which is missing.
"eighty in the second. They came from the westward": the text states a direction for these birds ("going N.E." also applies). Null is wrong.
The entry names no bird. "Larks" is copied from the context ("Larks at lantern"), while the checker used the section heading "Skylark". Both name the bird.

flags.why: "Blackbirds, Thrushes, Larks... at lantern...; a few killed": the dead birds are named. Give one observation per kind, not null and not the whole list.
"striking, 9 to 11 P.M. (156 Larks, twelve Starlings... killed.)": the bracket continues the clause, as in Example 1.
"from 7 P.M. to 3 A.M. (9th). Caught eighteen Thrushes...": a new sentence, so whether the time carries over is a matter of reach.
"A few birds at lantern between 9 and 11 P.M.; eighteen killed--... one Redwing": the continuing clause shares the time.
